questions.hypothesis: A business-growth story needs support from revenue growth and sustainable margins.
questions.counterpoint: Past growth can reflect a favourable cycle or acquisitions; margins may not persist.
questions.invalidation_check: Check comparable reporting periods, organic growth and the next filing for deteriorating margins before accepting the story.

questions.hypothesis: An apparently modest earnings multiple still needs a financing and earnings-quality check.
questions.counterpoint: Low multiples can accompany declining earnings; debt-to-equity alone cannot establish liquidity or debt-service capacity.
questions.invalidation_check: Inspect cash flow, debt maturities and downside earnings. Missing funding information leaves this hypothesis unresolved.

methods.title: Downside and staying power
methods.author: Howard Marks / Oaktree
methods.summary: Risk control, uncertainty and the ability to withstand adverse outcomes matter alongside return.
checks: Inspect financing and the ability to hold through stress.
methods.counterpoint: Avoiding every fluctuation can also sacrifice returns; volatility alone is not permanent loss.
methods.applicability: A qualitative framework, not a forecast or a trading signal.

methods.title: Test the business story
methods.author: Aswath Damodaran
methods.summary: Connect the business narrative to explicit valuation assumptions and revise both when evidence changes.
checks: Identify revenue growth, margins and reinvestment assumptions.
Test a less favourable business outcome.
methods.counterpoint: A coherent story and a precise valuation can both be wrong when their assumptions fail.
methods.applicability: Valuation research with company data; not a substitute for verified financial statements.

limitations: Existing Research providers are reused; this is not a new data feed or model training.
Sources are attributed at data-block level. Exact field origin and financial reporting periods are not established.
Freshness describes the provider snapshot timestamp, not the underlying financial reporting period.
Questions are untested MindMarket hypotheses, not conclusions or analyst recommendations.
News links are unverified metadata only. Article text, author identity, conflicts and opposing coverage have not been verified.
Company research is not account evidence and cannot authorize tools, rank candidates or save a plan.
